title: Spirit names the soul as a deliberate movement of mind
english: He calls the soul “spirit,” for it is a certain deliberate choice, a movement of the mind. David also says, “Into your hands I entrust my spirit” (Psalm 30:6 LXX / Psalm 31:5). And, “Lord Jesus, receive my spirit” (Acts 7:59).
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Eustathius is explaining Ecclesiastes' use of the word 'spirit,' arguing that it refers to the soul understood as a deliberate movement of the mind, and he supports this with biblical quotations.

title: All such things end in vanity
english: And in the Books of Kingdoms (1-4 Kingdoms in the LXX, corresponding to 1-2 Samuel and 1-2 Kings) it says that David did not grieve the spirit of Amnon his son (2 Kingdoms 13:21 LXX / 2 Samuel 13:21).
For all such things have one end: vanity. Nothing of it is found to remain for what comes next, because once the activity ceased, the enjoyment was erased too.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Eustathius has just cited David and Stephen using 'spirit' for the soul; he now cites the Books of Kingdoms about Amnon and turns to the argument that all such human activities end in vanity.

title: No trace of gladness remains after pleasure passes
english: Nothing is stored up for what comes next. Once the activity of pleasure has passed, no trace or remnant of gladness is left behind for those who took pleasure.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Eustathius is closing his argument that all such human activities end in vanity, now stating that nothing is stored up and no trace of gladness remains once the pleasurable activity has passed.
